prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE individual square PNG for a 30-pair ships memory game.
Primary request: a beautiful, accurate, finished COLOUR SKETCH of the single real named vessel below.
Input image: the supplied Titanic sketch is ONLY the approved drawing STYLE and warm ivory PAPER reference. Draw ONLY the new vessel requested below, do not copy Titanic's hull or funnels. Match its fine visible coloured-pencil strokes, delicate graphite contours, selective cross-hatching and restrained transparent watercolour modelling, softly lit from upper left. Expert maritime illustrator, richly finished yet visibly hand drawn, natural colours, paper highlights. No photographic, CGI, toy, cartoon or vector look.
Backdrop: uniform warm ivory drawing paper, subtle fine grain, otherwise BLANK edge to edge. No scenery, sky, ocean, horizon, waves, wake, ground, cast shadow or decorative wash. Show the vessel as a clean waterline portrait: only its above-water hull, with a neat lower waterline edge on blank paper.
Composition: Draw a modest-sized ship with VERY GENEROUS blank paper around it, like a small museum specimen in the middle of a large square page. The complete silhouette should span about 60% of canvas width or height, not more. SQUARE 1:1, at least 1024px. Exactly ONE complete ship, centred, with moderate three-quarter foreshortening so the long side and distinctive silhouette are readable. All extremities including bowsprit, mast tops, sails, cranes, stern and lifeboats must fit in the central 64% of BOTH dimensions. At least 14% completely blank paper on EVERY side. Do not enlarge it to fill the page. Keep the vessel upright with vertical masts; varied compass headings and viewing sides across this collection, NEVER a rolled or tipped ship.
Text: none. No names, letters, numbers, hull identifiers, logos, flags bearing symbols, labels, caption, signature, watermark or card border. Identification through major shape and colours. No crew, passengers, other vessels or objects.
Historical treatment: portray the vessel intact in its working heyday even if it was later sunk or retired. No damage, sinking, combat, smoke or explosions.
Specific vessel, identifying details and requested view: SS Great Britain. 1845 original six-masted iron screw passenger steamship. Low long black hull, white bulwarks, EXACTLY SIX slim wooden masts with spars and rigging, sails mostly furled so six masts remain distinct, one short buff funnel between the forward masts. No paddlewheels. View: port bow; bow lower left. Keep the whole vessel upright, centred and within the central 68% of BOTH dimensions, generous blank paper on every side.

edits.prompt: Edit this ship drawing ONLY to correct its scale on the page. Preserve the exact entire ship, details, colours, direction, geometry and fine coloured-pencil style. SHRINK the entire ship UNIFORMLY to 78% of its present size, centred on the SAME square ivory page. The whole silhouette including ALL masts and bowsprit must occupy no more than 70% of both width and height, at least 15% completely BLANK ivory paper on ALL FOUR sides. Seamlessly extend identical paper. No new objects, text, border, shadow, water or scenery. Also correct this specific historical detail while preserving the SIX mast count: SS Great Britain in 1845 was a SIX-MASTED SCHOONER, and only the SECOND mast from the BOW (the mainmast) carried square-sail horizontal yards. Remove the horizontal square-sail yards and their furled square sails from the OTHER FIVE masts. Keep those five as slim fore-and-aft schooner masts with fine rigging and small fore-aft booms, no full sails. Keep six masts total, single buff funnel, hull unchanged.

Correct this SS Great Britain sketch with exactly two changes. 1. There are currently SEVEN masts: REMOVE the very LAST (furthest RIGHT, shortest) mast entirely, including only its associated rigging, leaving exactly SIX masts. Keep all remaining masts where they are: the second from left has square yards, the other five have none. 2. Uniformly reduce the whole ship and all its six remaining masts to 86% of the present size, centred, with at least 14% blank ivory paper on left and right. Preserve the exact existing hull, single funnel, colours and pencil texture. No text, water, border or new details.

review: Full-size visually reviewed; whole silhouette, mast count, generous safe margins and hand-drawn style.
